## Substantive new finding

The Louisiana State Mineral and Energy Board's **certified 44-page November 13, 2024 minutes** include the complete first public **Opening of Bids** section. The public opening began at **8:30 a.m.** The presiding official, Angela Patterson, stated that **Tracts 45858–45872** had been advertised, **none advertised was withdrawn**, and **no letters of protest were received**. She read the offered bids; the opening pages enumerate bidding for tracts 45858, 45859 (two bidders), 45860, 45861, 45862, 45863, 45864, 45865, 45866, 45867 (two bidders), 45868, 45870, 45871, and 45872. **There is no entry for the advertised Bohemia Tract 45869.** On the last page the minutes state, **"This concluded the reading of the bids"**, and show the secretary's signed submission. All six public bid-opening page images were separately examined. The exact critical visible transition is **Tract 45868 on PDF zero-based page 5, then Tract 45870 on the same page**.

This materially narrows the prior v50e inference drawn from aggregate award acreage. We now have **contemporaneous tract-specific evidence that no 45869 bid was recorded as opened/read in this public session**. It is fair to report that absence. Do NOT state categorically that the state received no private inquiries or late/nonconforming bid, that an offer was rejected for a particular cause, that a lease was never later offered/executed, or that the 2024 event explains any unrelated 1920s–2015 claimant payment. The source lacks an explicit rejection notice or subsequent lease history.

**2024 tract reconciliation retained:** separate official notice for Tract 45869 names Robert A. Schroeder, Inc. as nominator, estimated **107 net mineral acres** on Orleans Levee District tracts 147–164. November 13 agency sale totals: **9 nominated / 481.553 acres**, **8 awarded / 374.553 acres**. Difference **1 tract / 107.000 acres**. Louisiana's November 14 press release lists awarded parish locations, omitting Plaquemines. The direct bid-opening minutes are now the strongest contemporaneous record for the **absence from the public bid reading**; aggregate arithmetic is corroboration.
